DetailsIngressDuplicateConflict.description:
`ingress.duplicate_conflict` (5.4.0, Esquadro): the same `message_id` arrived again and differs in
at least one COMPARED field. The answer is still 200 and nothing is executed; this entry makes it
visible (category ingress, actor system, outcome `info`, `safe_to_display` true). Expiry and
everything else keep coming from the FIRST receipt.
- Compared (closed list): `source`, `signal_type`, `action`, `position_effect`, `side`,
  `instrument`, `quantity`, `order`, `changes`, `refs`. The receipt keeps the sha256 of the canonical
  parsed JSON of these fields only (absent ≠ null, as in the schema), and only while the content
  itself is kept.
- Not compared: `message_id` (the key), `sent_at` (changes on every re-send), `reference_price`
  (changes on a re-send of the same bar), `details` (free text, never used by routing) and
  `schema_version`.
- Same compared fields → `ingress.duplicate_ignored` (200, no warning).
- Emitted only while the first content exists. The purge job (Q13-b) deletes the instruction and,
  in the same batch, sets the receipt's `body_sha256` to NULL and `content_purged_at`. A re-send of
  the id after the purge is a plain `ingress.duplicate_ignored` with `content_not_retained: true`
  (200, nothing executes), never this code (Esquadro, final).
A new instruction field joins the list only by an explicit contract change, here and in
`contracts/instruction/v1/README.md`. Never a body value: only the names of the compared fields that
differ.

message_id.description: As received; the Core refuses token-shaped ids at ingress.

limit.description: Money, or a percent string for consistency.

used.description: Money, or a percent string for consistency.

DetailsRoutingDecision.description:
Every `routing.*` decision code (routed, capped, skipped, refused, expired). Q74: for a `reverse`
the position check (ADR-0003 §4.2) runs before the entry gates. On an account barred for entries
(`out_of_sync`, `risk_blocked`, `limits_pending`, `no_bracket_profile`), or with no room
(`max_position_reached`, derived M = 0): position opposite → only the close leg runs, and the
entry carries the gate code, outcome `partial` (decision `capped`), `sizing.executed_qty` = 0
for the open, and `reverse_closed_qty`; flat → skipped with the gate code, no
`reverse_closed_qty`; already on the reverse side → `routing.position_conflict` (rejected and
notified, never a flatten). The same holds when the open leg of a reverse with an opposite
position expires at routing (gate `expired`, TTL; 5.1.0): the close leg runs (no expiry; audited as
late if it is), and the entry carries `routing.expired`, outcome `partial`, `executed_qty` = 0 for
the open and `reverse_closed_qty`; flat → outcome `expired`. Only at routing: when the routing decision itself sees the TTL exceeded (gate 10, e.g. a late webhook). An open leg that expires later, in the gateway queue while the connection is down, is not a routing decision: the decision stays `routed`, and ADR-0004 §5 applies ("Exception: the opening leg of a reverse", 5.1.1): the open is held until the flatten it depends on is terminal; if it then expires it is `expired`, audited as `execution.expired`, and it does NOT flag the account out of sync only when (1) it never left the Core, (2) the flatten succeeded with a proven flat position (`already_flat`, or for `filled` the latest report with `position_after` shows 0 and no later report exists), and (3) the account has no other sync reason; it then gets `routing.reverse_close_only` with `reason_code: routing.expired`. Any other case flags out of sync as before.

limits_version.description: With `routing.limits_pending` — the account's limits version not yet derived (ADR-0006).

reverse_closed_qty.description: Q74: abs(position) read at the decision, i.e. the quantity the close leg of a reverse is sent to flatten when its open leg is skipped with this code. The executed result is in the execution entries.

ParamsOptInSuspendedByFirm.description: `accounts.opt_in_suspended` grouped per firm and release (one notification, "{k} contas"); the audit keeps one entry per account.

ParamsPresetNewVersion.description: `presets.new_version` — one per firm (Q-S16-5): a newer release affects `account_count` of the caller's accounts.

ParamsReverseCloseOnly.description:
Q74 (Vigia I1): a `reverse` that closed the position and skipped the open, because the account is
barred for entries or has no room. Always notified, one per occurrence, whatever the gate
(including `routing.limits_pending`, which is otherwise not notified). It replaces the gate's own
grouped notification for that occurrence. The audit entry carries the gate code
(`DetailsRoutingDecision.reverse_closed_qty`).

reason_code.description: The gate that skipped the open leg; `routing.expired` when the routing decision saw the open's TTL exceeded (5.1.0), or when the open leg expired in the gateway queue under the ADR-0004 §5 reverse exception (5.1.1).

closed_qty.description: abs(position) read at the decision: the quantity the close leg is sent to flatten (as `DetailsRoutingDecision.reverse_closed_qty`).

closed_side.description: The side of the position that was closed.

SizeAmount.description: Account size in `currency` (decimal string, at most 2 decimals, > 0). Zero fails the pattern: 400 `common.invalid_request`.
